open_points.subject: file content digests
open_points.text: “Every content-derived identity and digest in this kernel is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the model's meaning facts” conflicts with file fields such as “content_digest” and “The body is described ... [with] the SHA-256 of its content”; arbitrary file bytes have no RFC 8785 canonical JSON form.
open_points.question: What exact bytes are hashed for a StoredValue file fixture, a SpooledFile, a trial file output and a multipart file-part content digest?
options: SHA-256 of the raw file bytes
SHA-256 of a canonical JSON encoding such as base64 text
Different explicitly defined digest rules for JSON values and files
open_points.default_guess: Use SHA-256 of raw bytes for files and SHA-256 of RFC 8785 bytes for JSON values.

open_points.subject: canonical_values.canonical_bytes
open_points.text: The operation takes “One JSON value” but must refuse “a duplicate key”; after JSON has become a value, duplicate object members may already have been discarded.
open_points.question: Does canonical_bytes receive raw JSON text or a lossless parsed representation that preserves duplicate members, and which layer detects duplicates?
options: Accept raw JSON text and parse it strictly
Accept a duplicate-preserving parse tree
Require surface and service_invoker to reject duplicates before passing an ordinary JSON value
open_points.default_guess: Use a strict duplicate-detecting parser before constructing the ordinary JSON value.

open_points.subject: content identity ordering
open_points.text: “Lists whose order carries no meaning are sorted before hashing — ... edges in the edge order of A05, constants by (`to_node`, `to_port`)”. Distinct guarded edges can have the same endpoint tuple, and distinct constants can target the same port.
open_points.question: What tie-breaker makes ordering, and therefore flow_version_id, independent of submission order when primary sort keys are equal?
options: Compare the complete canonical edge or constant after the stated primary key
Reject every repeated endpoint or constant target before identity computation
Treat input order as meaningful for tied items
open_points.default_guess: Use the complete canonical item as a final tie-breaker.

open_points.subject: A05 proof failure order
open_points.text: Edges are checked “by (`to_node`, `to_port`, `from_node`, `from_port`)”, but two otherwise distinct guarded edges may have the same tuple; constants are ordered only by (`to_node`, `to_port`) even though duplicate constants reach proof phase 6.
open_points.question: Which tied edge or constant is checked first and reported when tied items fail differently?
options: Tie-break by the complete canonical item
Report one aggregate failure for the tied endpoint
Refuse tied endpoints during composition
open_points.default_guess: Tie-break by the complete canonical item.

open_points.subject: ProofResult failure locator
open_points.text: ProofResult carries “the first failing edge or node”, while proof phase 2 can fail a constant and phase 6 can fail an input or flow-output port.
open_points.question: How does ProofResult identify failures whose subject is a constant or port rather than a node or edge?
options: Add typed locators for constant and port
Represent them by their target node and port
Return only phase and reason for those failures
open_points.default_guess: Use a typed locator with node, edge, constant and port variants.

open_points.subject: operation_element_conclusion
open_points.text: It returns “waiting with its reason and, for `owner_approval`, the `approval_id` ...; or not reached when the element has no NodeExecution yet”. An element awaiting its first approval also has no NodeExecution yet.
open_points.question: How is an unreached element distinguished from an element awaiting approval when neither has a NodeExecution?
options: Check for a requested approval before returning not_reached
Persist an explicit reached state
Treat every no-NodeExecution element as not_reached
open_points.default_guess: Return owner_approval when a requested approval exists; otherwise return not_reached.

open_points.subject: successful run with guarded skips
open_points.text: M19 says a run is “`succeeded` when every node and output concluded successfully”, while A13 says “`succeeded` when every node concluded succeeded or `skipped_by_guard`” and permits flow outputs reported `skipped_by_guard`.
open_points.question: Does a guarded skip count as successful conclusion for both nodes and flow outputs when determining the final run status?
options: Yes, skipped_by_guard is successful for run completion
No, any skipped node or output prevents succeeded
Nodes may be skipped successfully but every flow output must be produced
open_points.default_guess: Treat skipped_by_guard as successful completion for both nodes and outputs.

open_points.subject: approval request digest for multipart bodies
open_points.text: Owner decision 18 says approval covers “the fully built request ... headers and body” and “Any difference at send ... asks again”, but A10 excludes the multipart boundary from both the Content-Type description and body description so “equal parts give equal descriptions”.
open_points.question: Does a changed multipart boundary produce a different approved request or is the approval intentionally over the semantic parts rather than exact wire bytes?
options: Boundary changes do not matter; approve the semantic multipart description
Freeze the boundary and include it in the request digest
Any regenerated boundary voids the approval
open_points.default_guess: Freeze a deterministic boundary and include the resulting exact header and body bytes in the digest.

open_points.subject: approval request digest for header names
open_points.text: A10 says a difference in “a required header's name ... means the approval is no authority”, but the request description stores header names “lower-cased”, making case-only name changes indistinguishable; this also affects the credential header name.
open_points.question: Should case-only changes to HTTP header names void an approval?
options: No, compare header names case-insensitively in the digest
Yes, preserve original header-name spelling in the digest
Preserve spelling only for required and credential headers
open_points.default_guess: Treat header names case-insensitively and state that case-only changes do not void approval.

open_points.subject: multipart field names
open_points.text: Multipart parts use `Content-Disposition: form-data; name="<port>"` and file parts add `filename="<port>"`, but port names have no stated character restriction or escaping rule for quoted header parameters.
open_points.question: Which port names are legal in multipart bindings, and how are quotes, backslashes, non-ASCII characters and control characters encoded or refused?
options: Restrict multipart port names to a closed ASCII identifier syntax
Define quoted-string escaping and filename encoding
Percent-encode port names in multipart parameters
open_points.default_guess: Restrict multipart port names to a conservative ASCII identifier syntax during binding proposal.

open_points.subject: required HTTP header values
open_points.text: A required header value is accepted when it is non-empty, has no surrounding whitespace and no control character, and is then sent “verbatim”; non-ASCII Unicode is neither refused nor given a wire encoding.
open_points.question: Are required header values restricted to ASCII, encoded with a specified HTTP-field encoding, or allowed only when the selected HTTP implementation can transmit them?
options: Require visible ASCII plus permitted horizontal space
Specify UTF-8 bytes for header values
Use an explicitly named HTTP library's header encoding rules

open_points.subject: api_base_url validation and joining
open_points.text: A base URL is accepted when it is “an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host”, and the request URL is formed from “the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared path”; query, fragment, user-info and multiple trailing slashes are not addressed.
open_points.question: Which base-URL components are allowed, and is joining literal concatenation, RFC URL resolution or another normalization rule?
options: Require scheme, host, optional port and an optional path only, then concatenate after removing exactly defined trailing slashes
Allow all absolute URLs and define literal concatenation
Use RFC URL resolution with a specified normalization policy
open_points.default_guess: Reject user-info, query and fragment, preserve the base path, remove all trailing slashes and append the declared path literally.

open_points.subject: authored trial file fixtures
open_points.text: functions.add_trial_case takes “input values by port, optional expected outputs”, while file checking is defined only from “digest, size and media type” facts, yet the operation must publish fixture bytes through store.put_value_bytes.
open_points.question: How do the actual bytes of authored input and expected-output file fixtures enter functions.add_trial_case and associate with their declared facts?
options: Each file candidate carries bytes plus media type and the kernel computes digest and size
The request supplies bytes, digest and size and the kernel verifies them
A separate upload operation creates a fixture reference first
open_points.default_guess: Carry bytes and media type in the request and have the kernel compute digest and size.

open_points.subject: masked failure_detail length
open_points.text: For a classified execution, `failure_detail` is returned to an agent “only as its length and that class”.
open_points.question: Is length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points or another unit, and is it the original length or the already truncated stored length?
options: UTF-8 byte length of the stored truncated detail
Unicode code-point length of the stored detail
UTF-8 byte length of the original untruncated detail
open_points.default_guess: Return the UTF-8 byte length of the stored, already bounded detail.

open_points.subject: refusal reasons
open_points.text: An operation refuses with “a bounded reason naming the first failing check”, but most check names, reason grammar and whether request data may be embedded are not closed.
open_points.question: What exact stable reason identifiers or structured fields are returned for each operation-specific refusal, and may free text include caller-supplied values?
options: Define a closed reason identifier for every check plus optional sanitized text
Return unrestricted bounded human-readable text
Return the decision/rule identifier and check ordinal
open_points.default_guess: Use closed machine-readable reason identifiers and optional sanitized explanatory text that never echoes values.
